Subject: Renewal planning — increasing reserved capacity + long‑context model trial

Aditya / Redwood team,

Our annual renewal is coming up Oct 1 and we want to discuss expanding our Dedicated plan. Two drivers: 1) Product is shifting to a long‑context LLM for conversation history (we're evaluating a 32k context variant), and 2) adding a reranker stage to improve search relevance. Both increase GPU memory and sustained throughput needs.

Current committed pool: 40x H100 equivalent GPUs (reserved). We're seeing CPU and KV cache bottlenecks with the 16k model. Ballpark needs from infra: 70–80 GPUs once we roll the 32k model and enable reranker paths (reranker instances will be replicated across two pools).

Key asks for renewal discussion:
- Commercial impact for a bump from 40 -> 80 reserved GPUs (monthly committed rate + any upfront discount).
- Throughput guarantees / SLOs we can lean on for peak shopping hours (holiday window).
- Lead time for provisioning extra reserved pools and migration steps.
- Any model‑mix guidance: smaller quantized variants vs full precision and how that affects the GPU count.

Can we get a proposal and SOW addendum so procurement can triage before their Sept 10 steering meeting? Happy to do a quick sync early next week.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
VP Engineering — Folio Retail

Subject: RE: Renewal planning — technical sizing and model‑mix notes

Daniel — quick technical note on the sizing when introducing a 32k context model + a dedicated reranker tier: 

1) Model mix impact:
- Long‑context 32k model: memory footprint increases ~1.8–2.2x vs your current 16k variant (depending on kv cache retention). This increases per‑replica GPU RAM needs and reduces effective tokens/sec per GPU.
- Reranker: typically smaller model but higher QPS; we recommend running reranker replicas on a separate reserved pool (smaller GPUs/instances optimized for latency).

2) Recommended pool layout (staged):
- Primary gen pool: 56 H100 equiv GPUs for the 32k model (models pinned and quantized where safe).
- Reranker pool: 12 x A100/H100‑light equiv (optimized for latency) — this is a separate routable pool.
- Buffer/volatile pool: 10 GPUs for burst and testing.
-> Total recommended committed: 78 GPUs. This matches the commercial doc but lets us keep reranker and generation responsibilities isolated.

3) Performance levers to reduce GPU count:
- Aggressive 4‑bit quantization where quality tolerates it (saves ~30–40% memory).
- KV prefix caching: for conversation scenarios that reuse history, caching reduces recomputation; this needs workload‑specific tuning.
- Dynamic autoscaling policy: a reserved baseline + autoscale burst to a shared spare capacity for unpredictable peaks.

4) Timeline and on‑ramps:
- Provisioning: 3–4 weeks for reservation + config.
- Canary: 2–3 weeks to validate reranker QoE on live traffic at 10–25% traf.
- Full roll: additional 1–2 weeks after validation.

Attached: pricing_redline.xlsx with technical notes and per‑pool sizing. Happy to run a workshop with your ML infra team this week to calibrate numbers.

— Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
